709381.t: Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *snewbʰ- (“to marry, to wed”), and compared with Latin nūbō (“to marry”) (whence English nubile).

709342.t: Derived from νομίζω (nomízō, “to use customarily”) + -μα (-ma, “nominal suffix”).

709386.t: From Proto-Hellenic *nuks, from Proto-Indo-European *nókʷts (“night”). Cognates include Latin nox, Sanskrit नक्त् (nákt), Old Church Slavonic нощь (noštĭ), Albanian natë and Old English niht (whence English night).

709348.t: From νέμω (némō, “to pasture; to graze”) + -ός (-ós, deverbal nominal suffix). Compare ἀγρός (agrós).

709328.t: From νοέω (noéō, “to intend, to perceive, to see, to understand”) + -μα (-mă).

709302.t: Uncertain. Has traditionally been connected with νήχω (nḗkhō, “to swim”) from Proto-Indo-European *(s)neh₂- (“to flow, to swim”).

709319.t: Borrowed from Semitic. Compare Hebrew נֶתֶר (néṯer, “washing soda”), all ultimately from Egyptian nṯrj: R9

709390.t: Probably an enlargement in -τάζω (-tázō) of a Proto-Indo-European *snewd- (“to slumber, doze”); for the formation, compare κλαστάζω (klastázō) and βαστάζω (bastázō, “to lift up”).

709367.t: As if from *νουθέτης (*nouthétēs), from νοῦς (noûs) + τίθημι (títhēmi) + -της (-tēs), + -έω (-éō).

709387.t: Of unclear origin. Possibly from Proto-Indo-European *new- (“to make a push, nod”).

709398.t: From νωθής (nōthḗs, “sluggish, slothful”) + -ρός (-rós, adjective suffix). The origin of νωθής (nōthḗs, “slow, indolent, stubborn”) is disputed.

709305.t: From Proto-Indo-European *n̥-h₁d-tis (literally “having no eating”). Cognate with Old Armenian նօթի (nōtʻi, “hungry”).

709378.t: Related to νύξ (núx, “night”). Beekes compares the suffix to one in Latin nocturnus.
